location.label: Main Street & Park Street, Nashua, New Hampshire

assumptions.text: Road dry, as entered: friction 0.7 for the whole road (dry 0.7 · wet 0.5 · snow 0.25 · ice 0.1).
The road surface is flat. The terrain shown is for looks only and does not change the motion.
For the motion, vehicles are rigid bodies of typical weight for their type that don't tip over or break apart.
The dents show roughly where and how hard each vehicle was hit. They are drawn for illustration only and don't change the motion.
Each vehicle's resistance to spinning is that of a uniform rectangular box the size of its type: mass × (length² + width²) ÷ 12.

Vehicle A is treated as a typical car of 1,610 kg (3,550 lb), a class average. Source: EPA Automotive Trends Report 2025 (EPA-420-R-26-001), Fig. 3.6, model year 2024 class average, ±100 lb, read from chart: sedan/wagon about 3,550 lb.

assumptions.text: Speed at impact, as entered, and directions as entered. The picture works backwards from the impact for the 5 seconds before it.
No braking or steering unless entered: a vehicle not marked as braking keeps the same speed for the whole 5 seconds.

Simplified collision: the vehicles push apart along the line of the hit with a restitution of 0.2, and grip each other where they touch with a friction of 0.5, which can slow a vehicle hit on its side and turn both vehicles. Total momentum is conserved.

A push that lands away from a vehicle's middle, or the vehicles dragging on each other where they touch, starts it spinning. The spin slows at a steady rate set by the road friction and the vehicle's size, and the vehicle turns as it spins while it slides the way the hit sent it.

After the impact each vehicle is treated as skidding: it moves in the direction the hit sent it, slowing at the road friction × gravity (6.9 m/s²) until it stops, even where a vehicle rolling free would slow less. Any spin slows at a steady rate set by the road friction and the vehicle's size, and can carry on briefly after it stops sliding. There are no later collisions: a vehicle that would slide into another stops where they touch.
The motion is worked out in fixed steps of 1/120 s, so the same inputs always give the same picture.
Where a speed is "not sure", the picture uses the posted limit (around 25 mph, a typical city limit, if it isn't known), and the numbers shown run from 5 mph below to 5 mph above it.
